title: ChapterFlow Per-Book Over-Used Material ("scars")
description: One file per book, named <bookId>.json, listing the case phrases, prop/scene frames, and free-text notes that THIS book over-uses across chapters. The section-task builder renders these only into that book's writer prompts, so one book's scar tissue never leaks into another book's universal contract. Enforcement of over-use lives in the section/book gates (SEC/AS families); these lists are writer guidance, not a gate input.

phrases.description: Verbatim case-identifying phrases this book reuses (e.g. a named-case tag). Each may appear in at most one teaching unit book-wide.

frames.description: Scene engines, prop containers, or connective frames this book defaults to across chapters and must vary instead.

notes.description: Free-text reminders specific to this book's over-use patterns.

prohibitions.description: Non-negotiable rules for this book: reader-panel safety verdicts, and fact pins where surfaces contradicted each other. Rendered in their own block, BEFORE the over-use block, as absolute rules with no quota. Never file a safety rule or fact pin under phrases/frames/notes — those render under a header granting a quota of one and instructing the writer to paraphrase the item everywhere else, which for a prohibition means restating the banned thing in different words. Optional: absent means this book has no hard rules. CHAPTER SCOPE: a rule whose LABEL (the text before its first colon) carries a parenthesis holding NOTHING BUT chapter markers governs only those chapters and is rendered only into their prompts and repairs ("FACT PIN (ch03): ...", "FACT PIN (ch01, ch03): ..."); a label with no such parenthesis governs the whole book. Two shapes deliberately do NOT scope: a marker in the rule BODY is an illustration ("TIER CONTRACT: the tiers are standalone (ch01: the brother-break ...)"), and a parenthesis carrying any other word is PROVENANCE, not scope ("GRADUALISM CONSISTENCY (panel blockers, ch07): ..." governs the whole book). A label containing the word SAFETY is never chapter-scoped whatever marker it carries: reader-safety rules govern every chapter, because narrowing one harms the reader rather than merely wasting prompt. Re-scope a rule by editing its own label.
